cases.name: three-queued-then-one-ready
cases.detail: atm task assign fx-at10-beta ... --task-id at10-1789446761-1/2/3: assigned positions confirmed via `atm task list --json` as beta: [{"task_id":"at10-1789446761-1","position":1},{"task_id":"...-2","position":2},{"task_id":"...-3","position":3}]. `atm task events at10-1789446761-1 --json` showed handoffs kind=task_queued then kind=task_ready (trigger=task_pass); events -2 and -3 each showed only kind=task_queued, no task_ready. `atm list --pending-ack --json` as beta after each of the 3 assignments all returned {"count":0,"rows":[],"bucket_counts":{"pending_ack":0,...}} (unread climbed 1,2,3 but pending_ack stayed 0 all three times).

cases.name: close-releases-next
cases.detail: `atm task start at10-1789446761-1` then `atm task close at10-1789446761-1 completed ...` as beta. Polling `atm task events at10-1789446761-2 --json` at 1s intervals: task_ready handoff appeared after 3s: {"kind":"task_ready","agent":"fx-at10-beta","task_id":"at10-1789446761-2","trigger":"task_pass"} alongside events[].event="reminded" to_state=assigned. Well within the 30s bounded poll deadline.

cases.name: reassign-notifies-both
cases.detail: Assigned A (at10-1789446788-A, position1) and B (at10-1789446788-B, position2) to beta as alpha, then `atm task assign fx-at10-gamma "..." --task-id at10-1789446788-B --json` (same task-id, new assignee) as alpha. `atm task events at10-1789446788-B --json` showed events: [assigned(to fx-at10-beta), {"event":"reassigned","assignee":"fx-at10-gamma","from_state":"assigned","to_state":"assigned"}, reminded]; handoffs: [task_queued(beta), task_queued(gamma), {"kind":"task_closed","agent":"fx-at10-beta","task_id":"at10-1789446788-B"}, {"kind":"task_ready","agent":"fx-at10-gamma"}]. `atm task list --json` as gamma showed the task now assigned/position1 to fx-at10-gamma; as beta showed only task A remaining.

cases.name: move-head-readies-once
cases.detail: Assigned A (at10-1789446802-C4A) then B (at10-1789446802-C4B) to idle beta; polled A's events until task_ready handoff appeared (3s). Ran `atm task move at10-1789446802-C4B --head --json` -> {"task_id":"...-C4B","assignee":"fx-at10-beta","from":2,"to":1}. Post-move `atm task events` for A still shows exactly one handoffs[].kind=task_ready entry (no new one added). B's events show events[].event="moved" (detail "2\u21921") then exactly one handoffs[].kind=task_ready entry. `atm task list --json` as beta confirmed B at position1, A at position2.

cases.name: cancel-notifies-assignee
cases.detail: Assigned task at10-1789446824-C5 to beta as alpha, then `atm task close at10-1789446824-C5 cancelled "cancelling case5 task" --json` as alpha while still queued for beta. `atm task events at10-1789446824-C5 --json` shows events[1]={"event":"cancelled","close_outcome":"cancelled","to_state":"complete","assignee":"fx-at10-beta"} and handoffs[1]={"kind":"task_closed","agent":"fx-at10-beta"}. `atm list --json` as beta shows the delivered row {"message_id":"01M2HNF8CMFJ14GNRVT5DGX5TN","summary":"cancelling case5 task","from":"fx-at10-alpha","task_id":"at10-1789446824-C5"}.

cases.name: busy-assigner-sees-terminal-lines
cases.detail: gamma assigned at10-1789446838-C6alpha to alpha; alpha ran `atm task start` on it. `atm task list --json` as alpha then showed {"task_id":"at10-1789446838-C6alpha","state":"active",...} confirming alpha busy. While alpha stayed active on that task, alpha assigned at10-1789446838-C6beta to beta; beta ran `atm task start` then `atm task close ... completed`. `atm list --json` as alpha then contained, in chronological order (timestamps 04:34:02.053 then 04:34:02.061), rows {"message_id":"01M2HNFSP5WGBEXWCE7WZM12V8","summary":"beta starting alpha-assigned task","task_id":"at10-1789446838-C6beta"} followed by {"message_id":"01M2HNFSPDAB3XMJ8E4BJXZCXB","summary":"beta completed alpha-assigned task","task_id":"at10-1789446838-C6beta"} -- started strictly before completed.

cases.name: cleanup
cases.detail: All tasks closed via `atm task close` (completed/cancelled as appropriate) after each case. Final `atm task list --all --json` as alpha returned `[]`, confirming every member (alpha, beta, gamma) ended idle with an empty queue.
